---
title: "What are the lift and drag polars from −15° to +15° angle of attack?"
---


`AeroBuildup` swept across the whole angle-of-attack range, at a fixed speed.

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed
1. **Fixed 6 m/s**, the speed chapter 1 ran the BFG at, so the two chapters'
   polars are read at comparable Reynolds number.
:::

::: {#bb13dd20 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
alpha = np.linspace(-15, 15, 121)
p = polars(alpha, V=6.0)

LD = np.array(p["CL"]) / np.array(p["CD"])
i_best = int(np.argmax(LD))
```
:::


**Answer.** The best glide ratio on the polar is
6\.37:1, reached at
6\.0° (@fig-polars).

That is the polar's headline number, not the aircraft's. The glider trims
nose-higher than this and slower, so it never reaches the best-L/D point — which
is why the glide entry solves for trim rather than reading a figure off this
curve. Read this entry as the section's capability, and the glide entry for what
the airframe does with it.

::: {#cell-fig-polars .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(9, 3.0))

ax[0].plot(alpha, p["CL"])
ax[0].set_xlabel(r"$\alpha$ [deg]"); ax[0].set_ylabel(r"$C_L$")
ax[0].set_title("Lift curve")

ax[1].plot(alpha, p["CD"])
ax[1].set_xlabel(r"$\alpha$ [deg]"); ax[1].set_ylabel(r"$C_D$")
ax[1].set_title("Drag curve")

ax[2].plot(p["CD"], p["CL"])
ax[2].set_xlabel(r"$C_D$"); ax[2].set_ylabel(r"$C_L$")
ax[2].set_title("Drag polar")

# The best-L/D point, marked on all three so the same condition is locatable.
for a, (x, y) in zip(ax, [(alpha[i_best], p["CL"][i_best]),
                          (alpha[i_best], p["CD"][i_best]),
                          (p["CD"][i_best], p["CL"][i_best])]):
    a.plot(x, y, "o", color="C1", ms=6, zorder=3)
    a.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
